contracts: The focused Python selector invokes exact compiled C# observation cases through dotnet test and fresh TRX; exact case identity and runtime outputs bind each independent obligation assertion. Existing production entrypoints supply the observations. Missing classes/methods, build or startup harness failures, skipped/absent cases, stale/missing TRX and canned observations cannot be expected-red. Author tests only before the genuine runtime RED attempt; no new production helper is a required first-use entry. If existing behavior already satisfies an assertion, record that honestly instead of manufacturing a failure. Completion requires current positive and negative behavioral assertions; same-host tests certify no remote protocol or Windows OS isolation.
selector_intents: tests/s2_06/test_node_authority.py::test_o_0ac67bfae4d8 binds PhaseA.Platform.Tests.NodeIdentity.NodeAuthorityTests.O_0AC67BFAE4D8. Use a parameterized local-project write authority matrix at the existing production entrypoints; positive account authorization alone must not satisfy physical-node equality. Exercise WorkspaceStorageService.CreateSnapshot as a real project-file-writing boundary using a trusted RequestContext and existing protected project/workspace metadata, not a standalone test guard. For each mismatch independently assert the denial precedes file/path work and no execution or remote fallback is attempted. Include direct-service invocation so HTTP middleware alone cannot prove the claim; retain positive account-authorization controls. The matrix must cover current local project read/write entry families affected by these common owners; it cannot infer universal closure from a source scan or one canned boolean. Emit FAILURE_O_0AC67BFAE4D8 only for this actual behavioral mismatch. Use tests/s2_06/trx_support.py to invoke dotnet test PhaseA.Platform.Tests/PhaseA.Platform.Tests.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName=<exact bound case> --logger trx --results-directory <fresh temporary directory>, following the existing s10_fixture.py bridge. Require one fresh TRX, the exact successful C# observation case and valid typed runtime observations, then perform the bound Python behavioral assertions. The C# case records actual service results instead of asserting fake guard flags; Python failures must identify the violated assertion. A compiler error, missing compile-time owner/type/member, host-setup failure, unexpected test count, skipped case or invalid observation is test-harness-failure, never the behavioral failure token. Test observations must not depend on reflection proving a future member absent. Missing required ownership fields in an otherwise successful actual session response are valid negative behavioral observations; use safe JSON property inspection so their absence reaches the Python behavioral assertion.
